topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: It welcomes the students and establishes the overall importance and structural complexity of the complement system.

topics.label: Fundamental principles, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: They introduce the core properties, historical naming rules, and central molecular fulcrum of the complement cascade.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the upstream pathways that recognize pathogens and converge to reach the threshold of complement activation.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of activated complement
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the downstream actions by which activated complement destroys pathogens and drives inflammation.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect host cells from accidental complement damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the distinct disease manifestations and infection vulnerabilities resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen strategies for complement evasion
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the evolutionary mechanisms and molecular tactics used by pathogens to circumvent complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and preview
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
